## What it is

`screen_wedge` seated in `screen_base`. Both parts print flat and separately; this is
the only place the fit between them is checked. The wedge's rear plate lands on the
base's seat slope, its bottom face against the lip, its borders between the two rails,
and the base's two foot pins enter the wedge's sockets.

`slide` walks the wedge back up the slope so the joint is visible in the viewer.
Everything is home at 0, and that is how it checks.

Assembled at the default `tilt` 45°, matching `screen_base`'s own default.

## Design notes

- **The number this file exists to produce**: interpenetration between the two built
  solids is **0.000 mm³** at `slide = 0`. The wedge spans x ±63.05 inside rails whose
  inner faces sit at ±63.25, so 0.2 mm a side.
- The wedge is placed by a plane rather than by Euler angles: `Plane(origin=notch,
  x_dir=(1,0,0), z_dir=n)` has its own y running up the slope, so the wedge goes in at
  local `(0, wedge_length/2 + slide, 0)` and nothing has to be reasoned about twice.
- **Assembly floats arrive wrapped.** The runtime hands an `@assembly` its float
  arguments as a float subclass so the viewer can tie a slider to a hinge, and that
  wrapper does not survive being passed into `use()`. Hence the three `float()` calls
  at the top. Without them the build dies with
  `_Named.__new__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'param'`.
- `tilt` and `seat_height` are passed down to `screen_base` so the assembly cannot show
  a geometry the parts do not have. The wedge takes neither: it is the same part at
  every angle.
- The module is an `obstacle`, a plain box at its drawing size, glass flush with the
  pocket rim. It is there to show what fills the pocket, not to check anything.
- **`passe_cable` and `ecrou_passe_cable` are placed in the 16mm back opening**, gated
  behind `show_machine_face` (and `show_cable_gland`) since sizing the gland needs
  `machine_face_thickness`. The flange sits inside `screen_base`, against the back
  wall's own interior face (`north_y - back_wall_thickness`); the smooth barrel is
  sized with `epaisseur_a_traverser = back_wall_thickness + machine_face_thickness`
  (4mm: the 2mm back wall plus the 2mm machine panel, flush against each other with
  no gap) so the thread only starts once it has cleared both. `back_wall_thickness`
  (2.0) is a literal here matching `screen_base`'s own `wall` default, not derived —
  same pattern as `wedge_thickness` above.
- **The nut is screwed all the way down against the panel's inner face**, at
  `thread_start + ecrou_epaisseur` along the gland's own axis (`thread_start =
  bride_epaisseur + epaisseur_a_traverser`), consuming the first 5mm of the 6.5mm of
  thread and leaving `ecrou_passe_cable`'s own 1.5mm `amorce_entree` clearance
  exposed past it — the same split `passe_cable`'s own card documents (its 6.5mm
  filet is deliberately `ep_ecrou + amorce`, not a round number).
- **The 90° Z rotation on the gland is required for the thread to mate**, carried
  over from `ensemble_passe_cable` where it was measured (0.0mm³ interpenetration at
  90°, 12.5mm³ at 0°) rather than guessed; the nut gets no matching Z rotation, only
  the 180° flip about X so its lead-in cone faces the gland instead of the machine's
  interior.
- **`goujon_indexage` stops `screen_base` spinning about the gland's axis**, placed
  in the second (6x6mm square) opening 20mm to the right, since the far magnet alone
  doesn't grip hard enough to resist rotation. No Z rotation needed placing it — a
  square is unchanged by a 90° turn about its own axis, unlike the gland. `cle_longueur`
  and `fut_longueur` are overridden off `back_wall_thickness`/`machine_face_thickness`
  the same way `epaisseur_a_traverser` is for the gland, so both stay correct if either
  slider moves.

## Don't

- **Don't return the wedge pre-rotated from `screen_wedge`.** It is modelled rear-plate
  down because that is how it prints. The rotation belongs here.
- **Don't reintroduce `border_tb`, `cavity_depth` or `frame_th`.** They were hard-coded
  copies of `screen_wedge`'s numbers that drifted: `border_tb` was still 10.0 after the
  wedge went to 5.0, and the other two were left over from a frame plate that no longer
  exists. The wedge placed fine anyway because the old code leaned on its bounding box,
  which is exactly why the drift went unnoticed and the ghost module sat in the wrong
  place. Derive from `measured()` or pass parameters down.
- **Don't add a hinge.** Nothing here rotates. The wedge lifts straight out along the
  seat normal, and `slide` is a translation, not a joint.
- **Don't place a hole with `Pos(x, y, z) * Plane.XZ * Cylinder(...)` and expect
  (x, y, z) to land in world space.** Tried for the machine-face plate's two
  circles: `Plane.XZ`'s own axes permute the incoming `Pos` offset (z and y swap,
  one sign-flipped), so a Pos meant to put the hole's centre at world (ox,
  north_y, oz) actually put it somewhere else entirely, and the boolean cut still
  "succeeded" (right volume removed, wrong place) rather than erroring — the kind
  of bug `nurb check` cannot see. Build an explicit `Plane(origin=(ox, north_y,
  oz), x_dir=(1, 0, 0), z_dir=(0, 1, 0))` instead, the way `screen_base`'s own
  `straight_magnet_plane` does it, and confirm the cylinder's bounding box before
  trusting it.
- **Don't skip returning an `obstacle()`'d solid.** It is only added to the
  scene from what the function actually returns (`_flatten(result)`), same as a
  hinge — building it and calling `obstacle()` on it is not enough. The machine
  face plate is returned as `base + placed, plate`, a tuple, when
  `show_machine_face` is on.

## Changelog

- 2026-09-05: `goujon_indexage` (new part) placed in the 6x6mm second opening,
  20mm right of the cable gland, to stop `screen_base` rotating about the gland's
  axis — the far magnet's own friction isn't enough on its own.
- 2026-09-05: `passe_cable`/`ecrou_passe_cable` placed in the 16mm back opening,
  behind a new `show_cable_gland` toggle. `passe_cable` gained
  `epaisseur_a_traverser` (system.py's `passe_cable_body`) so its axial length is a
  parameter instead of a fixed `measured()` sum — it had no slider for its own Z
  length before this. Set here to 4mm (2mm `screen_base` back wall + 2mm machine
  panel) instead of the part's own 2.6mm default (1mm sheet + 1.6mm fond), since
  neither wall this crosses is the sheet metal the default was sized for.
- 2026-09-04: default `seat_height` 30 → 5, matching `screen_base`'s own default
  changed earlier the same day. Same stale-default bug as the `tilt` fix below —
  this one also matters now because `screen_wedge`'s new magnet wells are
  calibrated to `screen_base`'s defaults (see that card): at `seat_height` 30
  the two parts' wells no longer line up.
- 2026-09-04: default `tilt` 60° → 45°, matching `screen_base`'s own default changed
  earlier the same day. Left stale, the assembly opened on a stance neither part
  actually defaults to.
- 2026-08-17: rewritten around `screen_base`. Places the wedge on the cradle's slope,
  checks the fit (0.000 mm³ of interpenetration), and drops the stale hard-coded
  constants. Adds `slide` so the joint can be opened in the viewer.
- 2026-08-16: first cut, wedge alone stood at 60°, base out of scope.
